key_insight: Multimodal wearable-sensor models predicted perceived exertion better than pulse-rate-only models in patients with end-stage kidney disease (ESKD).
clinical_relevance: The findings suggest a potential approach to exertion monitoring during ESKD prehabilitation; this study concerns kidney disease, not cancer drug discovery.
method: Collected smartwatch pulse rate, electrodermal activity, skin temperature, and accelerometer data during prehabilitation.
Built individualized machine-learning regression models to predict Rating of Perceived Exertion.
Compared pulse-rate-only models with multi-feature models in ESKD patients and healthy older controls.
evidence_signal: Among 13 ESKD patients and 13 controls, multi-feature models significantly improved ESKD prediction, achieving a root mean square error of 1.33 RPE units.
watch_item: The small cohort and individualized modeling require broader validation before clinical implementation.
paper_title: Wearable Sensors Predict Exertion Without Changes in Pulse Rate for Frail End-Stage Kidney Disease Patients
